home.lead: pacs.008 (FIToFICustomerCreditTransfer) is the message one bank sends to another to move a customer's money. It says who pays, who gets paid, how much, and which banks are involved.
home.lead2: This guide walks through one synthetic example, from plain-language explanation to the raw XML.
home.start.title: Start here
home.start.intro: Six steps, in order. Tick each one when you finish it. Your progress stays in this browser.

xml.title: Annotated XML
xml.lead: Select any element to see what it is. Link straight to one with its path, for example #GrpHdr/MsgId.
xml.panel.empty: Select an element to see what it is.
xml.panel.none: No plain-English explanation for this element yet. The official definition below still applies.
xml.panel.choiceMember: One of several alternatives: only one element of this group is used in a message.
xml.panel.choice: A choice: exactly one of the elements inside it is used.
xml.legend.note: Required and optional are judged inside the parent: a required element is only needed when its parent is present.
xml.state.choice.hint: one of several alternatives, use exactly one
xml.mode.hint: Hides optional elements and everything inside them.
ws.resize.xmlTree: Resize the annotated XML and the schema tree
ws.resize.treeDetails: Resize the schema tree and the element details
tree.title: Full schema tree
tree.lead: Every element the message can carry, including the many the sample leaves out. Open a branch to load what sits inside it. Link straight to an element with its path, for example #GrpHdr/MsgId.
tree.search.hint: By tag, name or path, for example Dbtr or Debtor.
tree.search.error: The list of elements did not load. Leave the box and come back to try again.
tree.search.more: {n} matches, showing the first {shown}. Type more to narrow it down.
tree.required.hint: Hides optional elements and everything inside them. Choice alternatives stay, since one of them is needed.
tree.recursive: recursive: its contents are shown above
tree.any.hint: an open slot where other XML can be added
tree.occurs: Numbers in brackets, such as [0..1] or [1..n], give the fewest and the most times an element can appear inside its parent; n means no upper limit.
tree.constraints.lead: Rules that tie elements together, which the tree alone does not show. Each is given with its official name and definition.
